Thanks Susan — got the PDF and the notes. Attaching a short internal summary (redlines-notes.txt) for our team. Quick responses to your asks:

- Execution method: Redwood defaults to DocuSign for most customers (internal compliance validated). We can accommodate AdobeSign but it will cost a small manual step from our legal ops team. If FinHealth requires AdobeSign, please confirm and well escalate to ops.
- Breach timeline: 48 hours initial notice is aggressive. From a cross-customer operations perspective we typically commit to 72 hours for initial notification with interim updates within 24-48 hours as facts develop. We can include a clear escalation path and an SLA to push priorities.
- Subprocessor notification: we can commit to notifying customers of affected subprocessors within 48 hours of confirming subprocessor involvement.

Next steps: Aditya, can you draft proposed DPA language for the breach and cooperation sections that reconciles their 48h ask and our 72h practice (suggest "initial notice within 72h with immediate triage and 24h updates until stabilized")? Neha, please check whether we have any customers with a hard 48h requirement that would force us to accept their wording wholesale. Vivek, flag anything security/regulatory that must be included for FinHealth (PCI/FINREG mentions). Susan — well aim to come back with a reconciled redline in 48 hours.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Legal & Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — proposed compromise language

Team,

Drafted compromise language below for Marissa to review. Key points:
- Initial customer notification: 72 hours from detection for an incident that materially affects customer data.
- Interim updates: Redwood to provide an initial facts update within 24 hours of the initial notice and then reasonable updates every 72 hours until resolution.
- Subprocessor notification: Redwood will notify affected customers within 48 hours of confirming which subprocessors were involved, and will include the remediation steps taken by the subprocessor(s).
- Evidence/forensics: Redwood will retain relevant logs and make them available to the customer or regulators under confidentiality and as permitted by law; retention windows quoted in the DPA will reflect our current logging policy (90 days full access, 1 year restricted).

I also added an escalation clause: if the incident involves unauthorized access to regulated data (PII/PHI), Redwood's Security Lead will escalate to the VP of Prod Ops and the customer's security lead — contact info to be kept current on Schedule 2.

PTAL before I insert into the DPA draft.

- Aditya

Marissa, Aditya,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. FinHealth can accept 72 hours for the initial notification provided Redwood: (1) expressly documents the incident classification process in Schedule 2 (what constitutes "materially affects customer data"); (2) commits to subprocessor notification within 48 hours of confirmation; and (3) includes a cooperation clause for regulator requests — FinHealth needs to rely on Redwood to preserve evidence and make timely disclosures to support regulatory timelines.

Regarding e-signature: FinHealth legal will accept DocuSign if Redwood sends the envelope; they only asked that the audit trail be included in the final execution packet. If you can confirm DocuSign and provide the envelope link, we'll arrange for signatures on our side.

Assuming those items are added to the DPA, were aiming to sign by EOD Monday 17 Aug.

Best,
Susan
